passages.text: Phoenix rupicola (rupicola - Latin, inhabitant of rocks) or cliff date palm is a species of flowering plant in the palm family, native to the mountainous forests of India and Bhutan from {{Convert abbreviated|300 to 1200|m}}, usually occurring on cliffs, hillsides and similar terrain. It is threatened by habitat loss in its native range. On the other hand, the species is reportedly naturalised in the Andaman Islands, the Leeward Islands, Cuba and Puerto Rico and a specimen has recently been reported in Saint Lucia.{{citation needed|date=October 2014}}

Description
Phoenix rupicola palm trees grow to {{convert|8|m|ft}} in height, and {{Convert abbreviated|20|cm|sigfig=1}} in width. They are usually clean of leaf bases except near the crown.

Leaves are {{Convert abbreviated|2.5 to 3|m|ft}} long, {{Convert abbreviated|35|cm}} leaflets, pinnately arranged, on {{Convert abbreviated|50-60|cm}} pseudo petioles armed with spines. The spines are much less numerous and less vicious than the other Phoenix species.
The fruit is an oblong, yellow to orange drupe, {{Convert abbreviated|2|cm|sigfig=1}} long containing a single large seed.
